segments.text: As glucose rises, beta cells release more insulin, and it travels in the blood to cells all over the body.
In muscle and fat cells, insulin binds to receptors on the cell surface.
That signal moves extra glucose transporters, proteins that let glucose through, from inside the cell into its membrane.
More doors open, so glucose moves in faster.
In the liver, insulin switches on glycogenesis, which means building glycogen: glucose is joined into chains and stored.
